an-m64.name: 500 lb General Purpose bomb
an-m64.filler: TNT, Amatol or Comp B, ~260 lb (about 50% of weight)
an-m64.fuzes: Nose AN-M103 (inst./0.1 s); tail AN-M101A2 (0–0.1 s, 4–5 s, 8–11 s); long-delay M123/M124/M125 possible
an-m64.notes: The standard USAAF bomb in 1944–45 and the most common US Blindgänger found in Germany. Heavy bombers carried 10–12, fighter-bombers 1–2. In soft soil a dud may lie several metres deep, often deviated from its entry path (J-curve).

an-m65.name: 1000 lb General Purpose bomb
an-m65.filler: TNT, Amatol or Comp B, ~530 lb
an-m65.fuzes: Nose AN-M103; tail AN-M102A2; long-delay M124/M125 possible
an-m65.notes: Used against rail yards, bridges, factories and oil plants. Large duds can penetrate deep into soft ground.

an-m66.name: 2000 lb General Purpose bomb
an-m66.filler: TNT, Amatol or Comp B, ~1100 lb
an-m66.notes: Carried in small numbers by heavies against bridges, viaducts and heavy structures.

an-m57.name: 250 lb General Purpose bomb
an-m57.notes: Common on medium bombers and fighter-bombers in tactical attacks on rail lines, depots and villages.

an-m30.name: 100 lb General Purpose bomb
an-m30.notes: Used in mixed loads, often for area coverage.

an-m58.name: 500 lb Semi-Armour-Piercing bomb
an-m58.filler: Picric acid/Explosive D or TNT, ~145 lb
an-m58.notes: For hardened targets; rare over south-west Germany.

an-m41.name: 20 lb Fragmentation bomb
an-m41.notes: Dropped in AN-M1A2 clusters. Small, often lie near the surface; armed duds are sensitive.

an-m1a2.name: 100 lb Fragmentation cluster (6 × AN-M41)
an-m1a2.fuzes: Cluster adapter with mechanical time fuze; bombs fuzed AN-M110A1
an-m1a2.notes: Standard anti-airfield load of the Eighth AF. Expect scattered 20 lb frag bombs over large areas around airfields.

an-m81.name: 260 lb Fragmentation bomb
an-m81.filler: TNT or Comp B, ~34 lb, spiral-wound steel body
an-m81.fuzes: Nose AN-M103 / AN-M120 (VT proximity late war)
an-m81.notes: Tactical anti-personnel / anti-materiel bomb, medium bombers and P-47s.

an-m50.name: 4 lb Magnesium incendiary bomb
an-m50.filler: Thermate core in magnesium alloy body; X-variant with small explosive charge
an-m50.notes: Released from M17 clusters. Remains are found near the surface in urban areas; the X-variant can still explode.

an-m17.name: 500 lb Incendiary cluster (110 × AN-M50)
an-m17.fuzes: Cluster adapter with time fuze (AN-M146 type)
an-m17.notes: The Eighth AF's main incendiary load on towns and factories.

an-m47.name: 100 lb Incendiary bomb
an-m47.filler: IM/NP gel (napalm), PT-1 or white phosphorus
an-m47.notes: Thin-cased; WP-filled examples remain hazardous and may self-ignite when exposed to air.

firebomb.name: 75–165 gal drop-tank fire bomb
firebomb.notes: Used by P-47s against strongpoints and villages from late 1944. Remains seldom explosive; igniters may be live.

m8-rocket.name: 4.5 in air-to-ground rocket
m8-rocket.notes: Fired from P-47 triple tubes (M10). Rocket duds and motors turn up along roads and rail lines.

hvar.name: 5 in High Velocity Aircraft Rocket
hvar.notes: Used by Ninth AF fighter-bombers from early 1945.

cal50.name: 12.7 mm Browning machine-gun ammunition
cal50.filler: API M8, Incendiary M1, AP M2, Ball M2
cal50.notes: From strafing and air combat. Cases, belts and incendiary rounds are common surface finds.

an-m103.name: Nose fuze (impact, inst./0.1 s delay)
an-m103.notes: Standard nose fuze for GP bombs. A dud may be fully armed if the arming vane ran off during the fall.

an-m101.name: Tail fuzes (impact, short delays)
an-m101.notes: AN-M101A2 for 100–500 lb, AN-M102A2 for 1000–2000 lb bombs; delay elements from 0 to about 11 s.

m124.name: Long-delay chemical tail fuzes (Langzeitzünder)
m124.fuzes: Delays from about 1 h to 144 h; anti-withdrawal feature
m124.notes: The most dangerous US fuze in German clearance work: duds with chemical long-delay fuzes can detonate without being touched and must not be moved. Fatal accidents during defusing, e.g. Göttingen 2010.

raf-gp.filler: Amatol or TNT, low charge-to-weight ratio
raf-gp.name: RAF General Purpose bombs (early war)
raf-gp.notes: Used 1939–43 by Wellingtons, Hampdens and Whitleys; high failure rate, so early-war raid areas can hold relatively many duds.

raf-hc4000.filler: Amatol or Minol, about 75% of weight, thin steel case
raf-hc4000.name: RAF High Capacity 4000 lb blast bomb
raf-hc4000.notes: Blast bomb in nearly every Bomber Command area raid from 1943, also carried by Mosquitos. Duds are rare but very large.

raf-hc8000.name: RAF High Capacity blast bombs (larger types)
raf-hc8000.notes: Carried in small numbers by Lancasters and Halifaxes.

raf-inc30.name: RAF 30 lb incendiary bomb (phosphorus/gel)
raf-inc30.notes: Phosphorus-filled examples can self-ignite when exposed to air after decades underground.

raf-inc4.filler: Magnesium alloy body with thermite; 'X' type with small explosive charge
raf-inc4.name: RAF 4 lb magnesium stick incendiary
raf-inc4.notes: Dropped in hundreds of thousands in area raids; very common near-surface finds in German cities. Explosive 'X' types remain dangerous.

raf-mc1000.fuzes: Nose and tail pistols; long-delay pistol No. 37 possible
raf-mc1000.name: RAF Medium Capacity 1000 lb bomb
raf-mc1000.notes: Main RAF bomb against industry, rail and oil from 1943–45.

raf-mc500.filler: Amatol, RDX/TNT or Minol, about 40–50% of weight
raf-mc500.fuzes: Nose and tail pistols (e.g. No. 27, 28, 30); long-delay pistol No. 37 possible
raf-mc500.name: RAF Medium Capacity 500 lb bomb
raf-mc500.notes: Standard RAF high-explosive bomb from 1943; with the 1000 lb MC the most common British Blindgänger in Germany.

raf-p37.filler: Acetone ampoule acting on celluloid discs
raf-p37.fuzes: Delays from about 30 min to 144 h; anti-withdrawal device
raf-p37.name: RAF long-delay chemical tail pistol (Langzeitzünder)
raf-p37.notes: Fitted to a share of MC bombs in many raids. Duds with this pistol can detonate on their own and must not be moved or turned.

raf-tallboy.name: RAF 12,000 lb and 22,000 lb deep-penetration bombs
raf-tallboy.notes: 617 and 9 Squadrons only, against U-boat pens, viaducts and dams.
